current_content_summary: The user-facing integer theory, built on CoreInt (see that entry): re-exposes <, <=, +, unary -, *, and |_| as abbrevs over CoreInt's primitives, and derives binary - as x + (-y). Provides the standard ring/order lemma set (addzA/addzC/addz0/mulzA/mulzC/mulzDl/mulzDr, lez_trans/ltz_trans/lez_anti/lez_total, subz*, oppz*, and the usual monotonicity lemmas for + and < / <=); several induction schemes beyond the base intind (natind/natcase for non-negative integers, ge0ind/ge0case, intwlog/intswlog for 'without loss of generality' arguments, sintind for strong/well-founded induction); b2i (bool-to-{0,1} coercion) with its algebra; the IterOp theory (iteri/iter/iterop -- n-fold function iteration, exported); odd (parity) with oddD/oddM; the (soon-to-be-removed, per an inline comment) fold operator built on iter; and min/max with their standard lemmas.

import_repair_note: MOVED OUT, r2023.09 (commit-verified via library_history.json): `argmin`, `argminP`, `argmin_eq`, `argmin_le`, `argmin_min`, `argmin_out`, `ge0_argmin` and `minz` left Int for IntMin. Those are all 8 of Int's removals that release, so this is the whole minimisation API moving, not a partial split. The dependency runs one way only: IntMin.ec begins `require import AllCore Int.`, so a proof that writes `require import Int.` and uses `argmin` does NOT get it transitively and must name IntMin. Either `require import Int IntMin.` or replacing Int with IntMin works, since requiring IntMin brings Int with it. Apart from that one release Int has been purely additive since r2022.04, so any other unresolved Int name is a missing require or a name that did not exist yet -- not a move.
